summary.headline: Karamtara Q2 FY27 revenue rose 62% YoY to Rs 1,647 crore, with EBITDA margin at 11.9% and FY27 growth guidance of 60-65% kept unchanged.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 1,647 crore (+62% YoY), with 73% from international markets and 73% from renewable products. EBITDA was Rs 196 crore (11.9% margin, +46% YoY) and PAT was Rs 94.6 crore (5.7% margin, +37% YoY). H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 3,228 crore (+67% YoY), EBITDA Rs 370 crore and PAT Rs 182 crore. Management said margins should recover in H2 as higher freight and input costs are passed through, and reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 60-65%.

segments.name: Transmission towers and line hardware
segments.commentary: About 20% of Q2 revenue; management expects roughly 20% share in FY27 and a higher share from FY28 with Indian and Saudi capacity. Transmission towers supplied to over 50 countries, up to 1200 kV.

segments.name: Renewable products (solar, wind)
segments.commentary: Renewable products were 73% of Q2 revenue and 77% of H1 revenue.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: International was 73% of Q2 revenue (vs 45% a year earlier) and 70% of H1. US accounts for about 57% of the order book per management, and 66-67% of revenue over the last 1-2 quarters per analyst question.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 60-65% over FY26 unchanged; management says it is hopeful of meeting it despite Middle East freight costs.
Margins expected to improve in Q3 and Q4 as cost increases (mainly freight) are passed on to customers; Q2 EBITDA margin was about 100 bps better than Q1.
H1 typically contributes about 42-45% of annual revenue; H2 historically 55-58%.
Order book of about Rs 4,000 crore expected to execute in FY27 (about 60% of Rs 6,500 crore).
Saudi plant: revenue expected from next financial year (FY28), with a large contribution the year after; full capacity utilisation targeted by FY29-30.
Capacity utilisation expected at 60-70% by year end FY27, versus an optimum target of 85-90%.
Capex in FY27 expected at Rs 200-250 crore in the next half year, funded mainly by internal accruals, with term debt if required.
capex_capacity: Aggregated installed capacity of 8,79,800 metric tons per annum at quarter end, excluding captive rolling and galvanising facilities; management later cited 8,89,200 tons.
Capex of about Rs 370 crore in H1 FY27, versus about Rs 900 crore in FY26.

Bhachau (Gujarat) plant commenced production; new rolling mill and PEB facility for data centres targeted around the start of next financial year. PEB initial capacity about 100,000 tonnes; machines expected Jan-Feb, trials by March-April.

Saudi Arabia multiproduct plant (transmission towers and solar products): trial production expected December, galvanising plant commissioning targeted March; ramp-up 12-18 months. Commercial production next financial year.
Once Saudi and Bhachau are complete, sellable capacity to reach about 1.4 million tonnes (excluding captive profile mill and galvanising). Tower testing facility also planned.
demand_pricing: Order book Rs 6,500 crore at 30 September 2026, up from about Rs 6,000 crore at 30 June 2026; fresh order intake of about Rs 2,000-2,200 crore in the quarter.
Recent wins: Rs 1,200 crore of orders announced last month and a single Rs 550 crore US transmission order received the day before the call.
Management says US demand is robust (data centres, grid renewal) and Europe, Australia (anti-dumping duties on Chinese products) and Canada are growing.
Tariffs are passed through to customers; management says a 30% price gap versus US manufacturers leaves room for tariffs to be absorbed in pricing.
Freight on US contracts is pass-through; some Middle East contracts were on actuals and part was absorbed. Forex is naturally hedged by importing raw material for export orders.

Competition: China limited in US and Europe due to national security and quality/welding requirements; Indian and Turkish suppliers compete. Company says it is not bidding in tenders for India currently.

qa_highlights.question: Will transmission share rise and what is the receivables trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Transmission about 20% of revenue, roughly stable in FY27 and rising from FY28. Debtor days fell to 94 from 100 QoQ; higher international mix (73% vs 45% YoY) and Middle East transit delays lengthen cycles.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation and FY27 guidance achievability?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation expected at 60-70% by year-end versus an 85-90% target as new capacity ramps. Guidance maintained, with H2 seasonally stronger.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin still around 13% and what drives recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin recovered about 100 bps QoQ; higher freight (ocean and land, Middle East and elsewhere) and disrupted Middle East dispatches weighed. Cost increases to be passed through, benefiting Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why is H2 stronger than H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Monsoon slows infrastructure projects and deliveries are pushed to after September, so H2 historically carries 55-58% of revenue, with new capacity adding utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Defence subsidiary timing and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Still evaluating three or four scenarios in defence and aerospace; no guidance yet, as team is being built. Management is keen on both sectors.

qa_highlights.question: Saudi revenue and ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant almost fully constructed; trials by December-end, galvanising trials by March. Revenue starts next year, full-year contribution the year after, with full utilisation by FY29-30. No absolute revenue figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue CAGR and growth beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined a specific number; said growth would be decent, with 30-35% growth assumed off a larger base (FY26 revenue about Rs 4,300 crore).

risks_watch: Middle East disruption: port issues, higher freight, and paused dispatches that weigh on EBITDA; freight is at peak and quotes reflect current rates.
Working capital: debtor days at 94 and rising mix of international receivables with longer transit cycles.
Saudi and Bhachau execution: commissioning timelines (trials December, galvanising March, PEB machines Jan-Feb) and ramp-up pace.
US tariff policy (50% cited) and US concentration (about 57% of the order book); management says tariffs are passed through.
Capacity utilisation of only 60-70% targeted by year-end, versus an 85-90% optimum.
Defence and aerospace subsidiary has no defined timeline or revenue guidance yet.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, order book and guidance, while being cautious on near-term margins and freight costs. Management was vague on Saudi revenue quantum, defence timing and multi-year revenue CAGR.

adds.what: Bhachau (Gujarat) PEB / rolling mill facility for data centres, initial PEB capacity ~100,000 tonnes
Saudi Arabia multiproduct plant (transmission towers and solar products), commercial production next financial year (FY28)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth of 60-65% over FY26 (midpoint 62.5%) held, backed by a Rs 6,500 crore order book with ~Rs 4,000 crore expected to execute in FY27 (about 60% coverage of guidance) and H1 revenue already up 67%; capacity additions (Bhachau PEB, Saudi plant) are mostly FY28-driven, and management is only "hopeful" of meeting guidance given freight costs.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 11.9%, about 100 bps better than Q1, and management expects freight and input cost increases to be passed through in H2, with H1 margin at 11.5%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bhachau PEB/rolling mill targeted around start of next FY with trials Mar-Apr, and Saudi plant trials December and galvanising March, with commercial production in FY28; installed capacity of 8.8 lakh tonnes to rise to about 1.4 million tonnes once both are complete.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book of Rs 6,500 crore with about Rs 4,000 crore to execute in FY27 (about 60% coverage of 60-65% growth guidance), H1 revenue already up 67% YoY, and H2 historically 55-58% of revenue.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only expected at 60-70% by year-end FY27 versus an 85-90% target, so no new capacity need is pressing, yet FY27 capex of Rs 200-250 crore is guided for the next half year and management says it is putting up one more profile unit at Bhachau; a fresh announcement is possible rather than certain.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 60-65% was only held unchanged, with management saying it is hopeful of meeting it given Middle East freight costs; H1 revenue growth of 67% is above the range but H2 is seasonally larger.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management is only hopeful of hitting 60-65% growth despite Middle East freight and dispatch disruption, and H1 is 42-45% of annual revenue, so H2 must deliver the rest of the ~Rs 4,000 crore order-book execution.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Saudi multiproduct plant (transmission towers and solar) and Bhachau PEB facility for data centres start commercial output around FY28, but no product-specific launch dates or sizes were given; defence and aerospace have no timeline yet.

rows.label: Saudi Arabia plant ramp-up
rows.why: Trials by December 2026 and galvanising by March 2027, with revenue from FY28 and full utilisation targeted by FY29-30; no absolute revenue figure given.

rows.label: Fresh US and international order wins
rows.why: Order book rose from about Rs 6,000 crore to Rs 6,500 crore in Q2 with Rs 2,000-2,200 crore fresh intake, including a Rs 550 crore US transmission order received just before the call; US is about 57% of the order book.

rows.label: Debtor days normalisation
rows.why: Debtor days fell to 94 from 100 QoQ and cycle is 37 days, but higher international mix (73% vs 45% YoY) and Middle East transit delays may lengthen receivables again.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, order book and margin recovery in H2 and kept FY27 guidance, while being cautious on freight costs, Middle East dispatch delays and utilisation at 60-70%; analysts pushed on margins, receivables, and why H2 is stronger.
